newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-CHANG'S HOPES FADE IN HANOVER AFTER SECOND DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CHANG'S HOPES FADE IN HANOVER AFTER SECOND DEFEAT.

text.p: Michael Chang's hopes of reaching the decisive stages of the ATP world tennis championship suffered a major setback on Wednesday when he lost to Thomas Muster in his second defeat of the round-robin stage.

The American world number two, who lost his opening match to Wimbledon champion Richard Krajicek in straight sets on Tuesday, went down 6-4 6-3 after a baseline battle in the round-robin white group match.

The championship, which brings together the top eight players in the world, is played in a round-robin format in the early stages. The top two players from each of the two groups advance to the semifinals.
Chang reached the final of the season-ending championship last year but before that had a largely poor record at the event. The American now looks unlikely to go any further in the competition.

Like Chang, Muster needed a victory after losing to big-serving Croat Goran Ivanisevic on Tuesday's opening day. The Austrian took an early initiative with a break of serve in the third game which effectively clinched the first set.
After another break of serve at the start of the second set, the left-handed Muster managed to clinch the match in 87 minutes. The Austrian's final group game will be against Krajicek.
